library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Cardilin_2019_radiation_radiosensitizer_mouse"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Cardilin_2019_radiation_radiosensitizer_mouse"))$description`
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.1007/s00280-019-03829-y>

This is a preclinical tumor model for fractionated ionizing radiation combined
with a radiosensitizer (an anonymized small-molecule targeted therapy that
interferes with DNA-damage repair), fit to FaDu head-and-neck xenograft data in
mice. It extends the authors' earlier model
(`Cardilin_2018_radiation_radiosensitizer_mouse`, also in this library) to
long-term dynamics after treatment stops: tumor regrowth at a reduced rate,
and eradication.

* Untreated growth is **exponential**: proliferating cells `V1`
  (`cycling_cells`) grow at `kg` and leave at `kk` into a three-stage
  natural-death transit chain `V2`-`V4` (`damaged_cells1`-`damaged_cells3`).
* At each radiation fraction a fraction
  `F(D, C) = 1 - exp[-(1 + a C)(alpha D + beta D^2)]` of the proliferating cells
  is lethally irradiated and moved to `U1` (`irrad1`), which may divide once
  more into `U2` (`irrad2`, factor 2) before both die through the transit
  chain.
* The **accumulated effective radiation dose** `IR_Tot` (`irtot`) increases by
  `(1 + b C) D` at each fraction and permanently inhibits growth,
  `kg * exp(-gamma IR_Tot)`.
* `C` is the radiosensitizer plasma concentration at the time of irradiation,
  from a one-compartment model.

The tumor-static exposure (TSE) is the set of total radiation doses `D` and
radiosensitizer concentrations `C` at which the long-term net growth rate
`kg exp(-gamma (1 + b C) D) - kk` is zero.

# Population

Female CD1 nu/nu or NMRI nu/nu mice (five to six weeks old) carried
subcutaneous FaDu xenografts. Treatment started at a mean tumor volume of about
50-110 mm^3. Forty mice, ten per arm, received vehicle, radiation (2 Gy per
fraction), or radiation combined with 25 or 100 mg/kg of the oral
radiosensitizer 30 minutes before each fraction. Every arm was treated five
days a week (Mon-Fri) for six weeks, which is 30 fractions and 60 Gy in total.
Tumors were measured twice a week for up to 12 weeks after treatment stopped.
Radiosensitizer PK came from eight further mice (four at 25 and four at
100 mg/kg, sampled 1, 2 and 6 h after dosing). The source is the Methods
section, "Experimental data". The model was fit by mixed effects (FOCE) in a
Mathematica framework.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Cardilin_2019_radiation_radiosensitizer_mouse")$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lkg` (growth rate kg) | 0.40 1/day | Table 1 |
| `lkk` (kill rate kk) | 0.26 1/day | Table 1 |
| `lv0` (V1(0) = V0) | 27.0 mm^3 | Table 1 |
| `lgammaRad` (gamma) | 4.0 kGy^-1 = 0.0040 1/Gy | Table 1 |
| `lalpha` (LQ alpha) | 54.0 kGy^-1 = 0.054 1/Gy | Table 1 |
| `abratio` (alpha/beta, fixed) | 10 Gy | Methods, "Computational methods" |
| `lbRad` (enhancement of LQ kill; Eq. 3 symbol a) | 0.15 mL/ug | Table 1 row "b" (letters swapped; see Assumptions) |
| `lbRadTot` (enhancement of IR_Tot; Eq. 7 symbol b) | 0.42 mL/ug | Table 1 row "a"; Figs. 5 and 6 |
| `lke` (radiosensitizer elimination, fixed) | ln(2)/3 h^-1 = 5.55 1/day | Results, "Exposure to radiosensitizer" (half-life 3 h) |
| `lvf` (radiosensitizer V/F, fixed) | 11.95 L/kg | Fig. 3 peaks 2.09 / 8.39 ug/mL (digitized); text: 2 and 8 ug/mL |
| `radDose` (per fraction) | 2 Gy | Methods |
| `etalv0`, `etalgammaRad`, `etalalpha` | BSV 50%, 46%, 42% | Table 1 |
| `propSd`, `addSd` | 24%, 6.9 mm^3 | Table 1 (sigma a, sigma b) |
| PK `dC/dt = -ke C`, `C(0) = D F / V` | n/a | Eq. 1 |
| V1 growth and LQ transfer | n/a | Eqs. 2-3 |
| Growth inhibition `I = exp(-gamma IR_Tot)` | n/a | Eq. 4 |
| Transit chain V2-V4 | n/a | Eq. 5 |
| U1, U2 (one more division) | n/a | Eq. 6 |
| IR_Tot accumulation | n/a | Eq. 7 |
| Initial conditions | n/a | Eq. 8 |
| Net growth rate `knet` | n/a | Eq. 9 |

# Simulation set-up

Each radiation fraction is a unit bolus (`amt = 1`) into `rad_depot`. The
per-fraction radiation dose (Gy) is the model parameter `radDose` (default 2).
The radiosensitizer is dosed (mg/kg) into `central`. The observation
`tumor_vol` is total tumor volume (mm^3), and `knet` is the Eq. 9 net growth
rate.

The treatment schedule follows the paper's simulated figures (Figs. 3 and 5):
Monday to Friday for six weeks, starting on day 2. The paper's own simulations
evaluate the radiosensitizer effect at the peak concentration, so irradiation
here coincides with the radiosensitizer dose. In the experiment irradiation
came 30 minutes after dosing, when the concentration had fallen to 89% of the
peak.

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Cardilin_2019_radiation_radiosensitizer_mouse")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

# Typical-value solve for several animals at once. rxode2 warns that a
# multi-subject solve has no omega; that is intended here (each id is a
# different treatment arm, not a random draw).
solve_typ <- function(events, ...) {
  suppressWarnings(as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events, ...)))
}

# Typical values used by the closed-form checks below
kg <- 0.40
kk <- 0.26
gam <- 0.0040
alpha <- 0.054
beta <- alpha / 10
bRad <- 0.15
bRadTot <- 0.42
vf <- 11.95
ke <- log(2) / 3 * 24

tx_days <- unlist(lapply(0:5, function(w) 2 + 7 * w + 0:4))

make_arm <- function(id, rs_dose, irradiate, obs = seq(0, 130, by = 1),
                     rad_offset = 0) {
  ev <- data.frame(id = id, time = obs, evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = "cycling_cells")
  if (irradiate) {
    ev <- bind_rows(ev, data.frame(
      id = id, time = tx_days + rad_offset, evid = 1, amt = 1, cmt = "rad_depot"
    ))
  }
  if (rs_dose > 0) {
    ev <- bind_rows(ev, data.frame(
      id = id, time = tx_days, evid = 1, amt = rs_dose, cmt = "central"
    ))
  }
  arrange(ev, id, time, desc(evid))
}

arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm, ~label, ~rs_dose, ~irradiate,
  "A", "A: vehicle", 0, FALSE,
  "B", "B: radiation 2 Gy", 0, TRUE,
  "C", "C: 2 Gy + 25 mg/kg", 25, TRUE,
  "D", "D: 2 Gy + 100 mg/kg", 100, TRUE
)
```

# Radiosensitizer exposure (Figure 3)

```{r figure-3}
ev_pk <- bind_rows(
  make_arm(1, 25, FALSE, obs = seq(0, 60, by = 0.01)),
  make_arm(2, 100, FALSE, obs = seq(0, 60, by = 0.01))
)
pk <- solve_typ(ev_pk) |>
  mutate(dose = ifelse(id == 1, "25 mg/kg", "100 mg/kg"))

ggplot(pk, aes(time, Cc, colour = dose)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.4) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (day)", y = "Radiosensitizer concentration (ug/mL)", colour = NULL,
    title = "Replicates Figure 3 of Cardilin et al. (2019)"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## PKNCA check of the single-dose PK

The paper reports a 3 h half-life and peaks of about 2 and 8 ug/mL after 25
and 100 mg/kg. Fig. 3 draws these peaks at 2.09 and 8.39 ug/mL. The PK model
has no absorption phase (Eq. 1), so the peak is the time-zero concentration.

```{r pknca}
ev_sd <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(2), function(i) {
  dose <- c(25, 100)[i]
  data.frame(
    id = i, time = c(0, 0, 10^seq(-4, log10(1), length.out = 60)),
    evid = c(1, rep(0, 61)), amt = c(dose, rep(0, 61)),
    cmt = c("central", rep("cycling_cells", 61))
  )
}))
sd <- solve_typ(ev_sd, addDosing = FALSE) |>
  mutate(
    time_h = time * 24,
    treatment = ifelse(id == 1, "25 mg/kg", "100 mg/kg")
  ) |>
  distinct(id, time_h, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc))

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sd, Cc ~ time_h | treatment + id)
dose_df <- data.frame(
  id = 1:2, time_h = 0, dose = c(25, 100),
  treatment = c("25 mg/kg", "100 mg/kg")
)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, dose ~ time_h | treatment + id, route = "intravascular")
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmax, ~half.life,
  "25 mg/kg", 2.09, 3,
  "100 mg/kg", 8.39, 3
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Radiosensitizer single-dose NCA: model vs paper (Cmax from Fig. 3, half-life from Results).")

nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
stopifnot(
  all(abs(nca_wide$half.life - 3) < 0.05),
  all(abs(nca_wide$cmax / c(`100 mg/kg` = 8.39, `25 mg/kg` = 2.09)[nca_wide$treatment] - 1) < 0.02)
)
```

# Net growth rate over time (Figure 5)

The long-term net growth rate of the proliferating cells,
`knet = kg exp(-gamma IR_Tot) - kk` (Eq. 9), drops in steps at each fraction.
After the 30 fractions it has the closed form
`kg exp(-gamma * 60 * (1 + b C)) - kk`, where `C` is the concentration at
irradiation.

```{r figure-5}
ev_all <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(i) {
  make_arm(i, arms$rs_dose[i], arms$irradiate[i], obs = seq(0, 130, by = 0.25))
}))
typ <- solve_typ(ev_all, addDosing = FALSE) |>
  mutate(label = arms$label[id], arm = arms$arm[id])

ggplot(filter(typ, time <= 50), aes(time, knet, colour = label)) +
  geom_step(linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (day)", y = "Net growth rate (1/day)", colour = NULL,
    title = "Replicates Figure 5 of Cardilin et al. (2019)"
  ) +
  theme_bw()

end_knet <- typ |>
  filter(time == 50) |>
  select(arm, knet)
c_peak <- c(A = 0, B = 0, C = 25 / vf, D = 100 / vf)
irr <- c(A = 0, B = 1, C = 1, D = 1)
closed <- kg * exp(-gam * 60 * irr * (1 + bRadTot * c_peak)) - kk
fig5 <- tibble::tibble(
  arm = names(closed),
  simulated = end_knet$knet[match(names(closed), end_knet$arm)],
  closed_form = unname(closed),
  figure_5 = c(0.14, 0.054, -0.006, -0.127)
)
fig5 |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 4))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Arm" = arm,
    "Simulated knet at day 50 (1/day)" = simulated,
    "Closed form (1/day)" = closed_form,
    "Fig. 5, digitized (1/day)" = figure_5
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "End-of-treatment net growth rate by arm.")

stopifnot(
  # The solve against its own closed form: only the finite width of the
  # radiation spike separates them.
  all(abs(fig5$simulated - fig5$closed_form) < 0.002),
  # Against the published figure, read to about +/- 0.003 1/day.
  all(abs(fig5$simulated - fig5$figure_5) < 0.006)
)
```

Radiation alone (B) leaves a positive net growth rate, so the tumor regrows.
With 25 mg/kg (C) the rate only just turns negative, and with 100 mg/kg (D) it
is clearly negative. These match the paper's narrative and Figure 5. The
agreement also confirms which Table 1 potency belongs to the long-term effect
(see Assumptions).

# Tumor static exposure curve (Figure 6)

Setting `knet = 0` gives the TSE curve `D = log(kg / kk) / (gamma (1 + b C))`
(Eqs. 10-11, with the long-term parameters `gamma` and `b`). The points below
were digitized from the curve in Fig. 6 (left).

```{r figure-6}
tse <- function(C) log(kg / kk) / (gam * (1 + bRadTot * C))
fig6 <- tibble::tibble(
  C = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14.5),
  D_fig6 = c(74.6, 57.2, 46.7, 39.3, 30.0, 24.1, 20.0, 17.3, 14.7)
) |>
  mutate(D_model = tse(C), pct_diff = 100 * (D_model - D_fig6) / D_fig6)

ggplot(data.frame(C = seq(0, 15, by = 0.05)), aes(C, tse(C))) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = fig6, aes(C, D_fig6), shape = 1, size = 2) +
  labs(
    x = "Radiosensitizer concentration at irradiation (ug/mL)",
    y = "Total radiation dose (Gy)",
    title = "Replicates Figure 6 (left) of Cardilin et al. (2019)",
    caption = "Line: model TSE curve. Circles: digitized from Fig. 6."
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 120)) +
  theme_bw()

knitr::kable(
  fig6 |>
    mutate(across(c(D_model, pct_diff), \(x) round(x, 1))) |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "C (ug/mL)" = C, "D, Fig. 6 (Gy)" = D_fig6,
      "D, model (Gy)" = D_model, "% diff" = pct_diff
    ),
  caption = "TSE curve: model vs digitized Fig. 6."
)
stopifnot(all(abs(fig6$pct_diff) < 6))
```

For radiation alone the model needs `r round(tse(0), 1)` Gy in total. The
abstract and Discussion give 110 Gy, and Fig. 6 crosses the dose axis at about
107 Gy.

The simulation below checks that the ODE solution sits on this curve. The
radiosensitizer is dosed so that its concentration at each fraction is
`C = 4` ug/mL, and the 30 fractions together deliver exactly the TSE dose at
that concentration. Once the last fraction is given, the net growth rate
should be zero and the tumor should stop changing (the "B" trajectory of
Fig. 6, right).

```{r tse-stasis}
C_target <- 4
d_tse <- tse(C_target)
ev_stasis <- make_arm(1, C_target * vf, TRUE, obs = seq(0, 160, by = 0.5))
st <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_stasis,
  params = c(radDose = d_tse / 30), addDosing = FALSE
))

ggplot(st, aes(time, tumor_vol)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (day)", y = expression("Tumor volume (mm"^3 * ")"),
    title = "Exposure on the TSE curve gives tumor stasis (cf. Figure 6, right)",
    caption = sprintf("%.1f Gy total in 30 fractions with C = %g ug/mL at each fraction.", d_tse, C_target)
  ) +
  theme_bw()

knet_after <- st$knet[st$time == 60]
v_late <- st$tumor_vol[st$time %in% c(120, 160)]
stopifnot(
  abs(knet_after) < 1e-3,
  abs(v_late[2] / v_late[1] - 1) < 0.02
)
```

# Kill per radiation fraction

The Results section reports the percentage of proliferating cells killed by
one 2 Gy fraction. The table compares the simulated drop in `cycling_cells`
across a single fraction with the closed form `F(D, C)` and with the paper's
text.

```{r kill-fractions}
kill_one <- function(rs_dose) {
  ev <- data.frame(
    id = 1, time = c(0.999, 1.004), evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = "cycling_cells"
  )
  ev <- bind_rows(ev, data.frame(id = 1, time = 1, evid = 1, amt = 1, cmt = "rad_depot"))
  if (rs_dose > 0) {
    ev <- bind_rows(ev, data.frame(id = 1, time = 1, evid = 1, amt = rs_dose, cmt = "central"))
  }
  ev <- arrange(ev, time, desc(evid))
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev, addDosing = FALSE, atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10))
  100 * (1 - s$cycling_cells[2] / s$cycling_cells[1])
}
f_closed <- function(C) 100 * (1 - exp(-(1 + bRad * C) * (alpha * 2 + beta * 4)))
kill_tab <- tibble::tibble(
  scenario = c("2 Gy alone", "2 Gy + 25 mg/kg", "2 Gy + 100 mg/kg"),
  dose = c(0, 25, 100)
) |>
  mutate(
    simulated = sapply(dose, kill_one),
    closed_form = f_closed(dose / vf),
    paper_text = c(15, 19, 25)
  )
kill_tab |>
  select(-dose) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 1))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Scenario" = scenario,
    "Simulated kill (%)" = simulated,
    "Closed form F(D, C) (%)" = closed_form,
    "Paper text (%)" = paper_text
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Proliferating cells killed per 2 Gy fraction.")
stopifnot(all(abs(kill_tab$simulated - kill_tab$closed_form) < 0.5))
```

The model reproduces the 25% quoted for 100 mg/kg. It falls below the 15% and
19% quoted for radiation alone and for 25 mg/kg, which the text derives from an
alpha of 0.082 1/Gy that does not match Table 1 (see Assumptions).

# Visual predictive check (Figure 9)

For each arm, 100 virtual mice were simulated with between-subject variability
on `V0`, `gamma` and `alpha`. The plot shows the 10th, 50th and 90th
percentiles of tumor volume (individual predictions, no residual error).

```{r vpc}
n_per_arm <- 100
ev_vpc <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(i) {
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n_per_arm), function(j) {
    make_arm((i - 1) * n_per_arm + j, arms$rs_dose[i], arms$irradiate[i],
      obs = seq(0, 130, by = 2)
    )
  }))
}))
vpc <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_vpc, addDosing = FALSE)) |>
  mutate(
    arm_i = (id - 1) %/% n_per_arm + 1,
    label = arms$label[arm_i], arm = arms$arm[arm_i]
  )

vpc_sum <- vpc |>
  group_by(label, time) |>
  summarise(
    p10 = quantile(tumor_vol, 0.1), p50 = median(tumor_vol),
    p90 = quantile(tumor_vol, 0.9), .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(vpc_sum, aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p10, ymax = p90), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "steelblue4", linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~label, scales = "free_y") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (day)", y = expression("Tumor volume (mm"^3 * ")"),
    title = "Simulated percentiles by arm (cf. Figures 4, 8 and 9)",
    caption = "Median and 10th-90th percentile band of individual predictions; n = 100 per arm."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Eradication by arm

A tumor is eventually eradicated when its net growth rate after treatment is
negative, `gamma_i > log(kg / kk) / IR_Tot`. Only `gamma` carries
between-subject variability in this condition (log-normal, standard deviation
0.46), so the expected eradicated fraction has a closed form. The table
compares it with the simulated cohort and with the outcomes the paper reports
(Results: regrowth in 7/9 irradiated mice, eradication in 6/9 at 25 mg/kg and
in all mice at 100 mg/kg).

```{r eradication}
ir_tot <- c(B = 60, C = 60 * (1 + bRadTot * 25 / vf), D = 60 * (1 + bRadTot * 100 / vf))
p_erad <- 1 - pnorm(log(log(kg / kk) / ir_tot / gam) / 0.46)
sim_erad <- vpc |>
  filter(time == 60, arm != "A") |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(simulated = mean(knet < 0), .groups = "drop")
erad <- tibble::tibble(
  arm = names(p_erad), expected = unname(p_erad),
  observed = c(2 / 9, 6 / 9, 1)
) |>
  left_join(sim_erad, by = "arm")
erad |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(100 * x))) |>
  select(arm, expected, simulated, observed) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Arm" = arm,
    "Expected (%), closed form" = expected,
    "Simulated cohort (%)" = simulated,
    "Observed (%)" = observed
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Fraction of mice with eventual tumor eradication.")
stopifnot(
  all(abs(erad$simulated - erad$expected) < 0.15),
  p_erad[["B"]] < 0.3, p_erad[["C"]] > 0.4, p_erad[["D"]] > 0.9
)
```

The model matches the observed pattern: most irradiated tumors regrow, about
half to two-thirds are eradicated at 25 mg/kg, and nearly all at 100 mg/kg.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Radiosensitizer potency letters.** Eq. 3 calls the potency on the
  LQ kill `a` and Eq. 7 calls the potency on the accumulated dose `b`.
  Table 1 lists `a = 0.42` and `b = 0.15` mL/ug, and the TSE derivation
  (Eqs. 10-13) uses `a` for the long-term effect. The model's simulated
  figures settle which value goes where. Only 0.42 on the accumulated dose
  reproduces the TSE curve of Fig. 6 (about 58 Gy at 2 ug/mL and 15 Gy at
  15 ug/mL) and the end-of-treatment net growth rates of Fig. 5. With 0.15
  there, curve C would stay at about +0.03 1/day instead of turning slightly
  negative. The packaged model therefore uses 0.42 mL/ug on `IR_Tot`
  (`lbRadTot`) and 0.15 mL/ug on the LQ kill (`lbRad`). This also matches
  the reported 25% kill per fraction at 100 mg/kg. The same Table 1 letter
  swap occurs in the authors' 2018 paper.
- **Eqs. 9-13 typography.** Eq. 9 prints `exp(-alpha IR_Tot)` and Eq. 13
  prints `alpha`. By Eq. 4 the long-term inhibition uses `gamma`, and only
  `gamma` reproduces the 107.7 Gy radiation-alone TSE (110 Gy in the abstract
  and Discussion). Eq. 11 also has a misplaced fraction bar.
- **Results-section prose disagrees with Table 1.** The Results text quotes
  `alpha = 0.082 1/Gy` and a long-term parameter of `0.0034 1/Gy`. It also
  quotes a TSE of 120 Gy for radiation alone and 80 / 30 Gy for 25 / 100 mg/kg,
  and per-fraction kills of 15 / 19 / 25%. Table 1 gives `alpha = 54 kGy^-1`
  (0.054 1/Gy) and `gamma = 4.0 kGy^-1` (0.004 1/Gy). These Table 1 values
  reproduce the abstract (110 Gy) and Figs. 5 and 6, so the packaged model
  uses Table 1. The prose values seem to come from a different parameter set,
  and they disagree with each other as well as with the figures.
- **Median initial tumor volume.** The text gives a median initial volume of
  81 mm^3. With Eq. 8 and Table 1 (`V0 = 27`, `kk / kg = 0.65`) the initial
  total volume is 63.4 mm^3, which agrees with the starting point of the
  simulated trajectories in Fig. 6 (right). The packaged model follows Eq. 8
  and Table 1.
- **Radiosensitizer PK.** The paper gives no PK parameter estimates, only the
  one-compartment form without absorption (Eq. 1), a 3 h half-life, and peaks
  of about 2 and 8 ug/mL. `ke` is ln(2)/3 per hour. `V/F` = 11.95 L/kg comes
  from the peaks drawn in Fig. 3 (2.09 and 8.39 ug/mL, digitized by the
  maintainers; their ratio is 4.0, consistent with linear PK). The text's
  rounded peaks would give 12.5 L/kg. Both PK parameters are fixed, because
  the tumor model used them as an input. No PK variability is reported, so
  none is included.
- **Concentration at irradiation.** In the experiment irradiation followed
  dosing by 30 minutes. The paper's simulated figures (Figs. 5 and 6) evaluate
  the radiosensitizer at its peak, so the vignette doses and irradiates at the
  same time. To reproduce the experimental timing, offset the `rad_depot`
  events by 30 min (`make_arm(..., rad_offset = 0.5 / 24)`). The paper does
  not say which timing the estimation used.
- **Between-subject variability scale.** Table 1 gives BSV as a percentage
  without defining it. The model uses variance = (BSV/100)^2, the
  `sqrt(omega^2) x 100` definition stated in the footnote of the same group's
  2018 paper, which used the same Mathematica framework. Under the
  alternative `log(1 + CV^2)` definition the variances would be about 10%
  smaller.
- **Residual error.** Table 1 lists a proportional (24%) and an additive
  (6.9 mm^3) component without giving the combination rule. They are encoded
  as nlmixr2's combined `add(addSd) + prop(propSd)`.
- **Instantaneous radiation effects.** The jumps of Eqs. 2, 6 and 7 at each
  fraction are implemented with a fast-decaying trigger compartment
  (`rad_depot`, rate `krad = 5000` per day). Its integral is 1 per fraction,
  so the kill hazard integrates to the LQ lethal-lesion number and `irtot`
  rises by `(1 + b C) D`. The radiosensitizer concentration changes by about
  0.1% during the spike. The closed-form checks above show the remaining
  error.
- **Schedule.** The paper's figures start treatment on day 2 and treat on
  weekdays for six weeks. The vignette uses the same schedule. The observed
  data in Figs. 4, 8 and 9 are plotted from the start of treatment.
